items.title: Show HN: What is localhost? An interactive guide
items.summary: I've build whatislocalhost.com to showcase an app deployed to cloudish.ai -- Why? Well, I can either buy ads and brain wash people or, I can burn time, tokens and effort creating value for the community, we chose the latter :) The last year our team at Hal9 has been helping a bunch of founders that vibe-coded apps turn them into real MVPs (Minimum Viable Products) and then real products that scale in usage and revenue. One of the top questions we get was: why can't I just use my Claude Coded app as my website? Well, technically you can, but as many of you in HN already know, not the best idea. Computers go to sleep, are more likely to get hacked with exposed ports, have slow and unreliable internet, you only have one, and if you are doing heavy work it will slowdown your website. Therefore, I created https://whatislocalhost.com , which i an interactive explanation into what is localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 Hope this is useful to some, or at least insightful. items.title: Show HN: Git Hook for Model Identifation
items.summary: I have started using multiple models (Claude, Codex, Grok via cursor-agent, Z.ai, Deepseek, Hy4 via OpenCode, agy) etc, and I realized that I not able to identify which commit was made by which model. After looking around and not finding anything, I create a format specification that will let Model self-identify itself. The goal is a higher ranked model can verify the output of other models and suggest changes. It is similar how to a Senior Engineer will review the output of Junior Engineers. As Humans, we know which model is behaving well, and which we can trust more. My AI based commits have a identification like this. Add retry backoff to fetch Model: claude-sonnet-5-5 harness=claude-code effort=high conf=medium Model: opencode/hy4-flash-free harness=opencode effort=high conf=medium In using this, I get an intuition what I can expect when I fire off model on a particular task. items.title: Show HN: Zpup – Zdog style 3D scenes in JSON, SVG from any angle
items.summary: Hi. I made small project called Zpup. It takes small 3D scene written in JSON and gives back a flat SVG from any angle. There is no JavaScript in the file, so it works in img-tag or README. I needed 3D for small project at my company, and Zdog make big impression on me. But Zdog has not had a release for several years, so I wanted to make modern version. One thing works different. Zdog sorts each shape by one point. so small thing on big floor gets covered when you turn it. Zpup compares the shapes that overlap. You can see both in the README. I wrote it with Claude Code Fable 5.2. No canvas renderer, no text shape, and it is 0.2 version. Playground: https://rxolve.github.io/zpup Feedback is always welcome :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50556534 Points: 3 # Comments: 0
